objective: one computation objective at member granularity, with no group cells, at one link: the fourteen subtracting answers' rows that write the sign are each asked, at feed-forward 33's merge, for the movement that takes their features to the feature-increment target T^phi made against the seven original supports; every correct fitting member's own error against its ORIGINAL computation stands in the same sum at every place and every prompt position, direction and size, at that merge and at layer 33's last merge; every other row of a wrong member is an unsupported cell and carries no term

chain.order: one link: feed-forward 33, from the original.
chain.source_run_role: Read its original-derived bindings, membership, layout and baseline only. Its edited model and edited rows are no state of this chain.

first_rows.read_by: sign-request-at-33-original's own declared `rows` command on November 13, 2026, 12:24:03 to 12:26:12 AM CT, card 0 under its lock (that run's logs/rows-3.out and logs/run.log); that run makes no candidate and is preserved as it is
first_rows.why: the first link starts from the original, and a pass of the recorded text through the original at this matrix does not depend on the construction: the same rows, read once

chain.bindings_note: each is a feed-forward's output projection alone; every norm weight and output scale stays the original's bytes
chain.each_link: rows: the thirty fitting answers' recorded text once through the state the link starts from, at this link's matrix: its input and the state its merge adds to. At the first link (33) that state is the original and the rows are the ones `first_rows` names, read by another run; no pass is made again. asked: this link's request, from those rows and the original file's own reading, with its hash. candidate: this link's matrix solved on the declared sum. write: the candidate into the run's one file, then the whole file checked. Each keeps its record in links/<link>/: asked.npz and asked.json, candidate/, written.json.

33: feedforward-33: the matrix's own merge (the fourteen requests, and every correct member's own error)
layer-33: the layer's last merge behind it, read raw as the reference reads it (every correct member's own error; no request)

chain.closing: model/written.json is laid by `finished` only when its one link has their record: the file's hash, the matrices written and every link's record. Until then the file is a state under construction and no reader starts on it. A link whose selection keeps the start writes nothing.

correct_members.read_by: correction.candidate, which hands them to correction.chosen (charges, replaced): each correct member's own movement from its ORIGINAL computation on the same recorded text, at every registered place and every prompt position, at the link's two frames. At a later link the rows are the prefix's and what they are counted from stays the original file's own output at the same row: the term is the error against the original reference, not movement from the edited prefix.

row_requests.construction: feature-increment (Astra's T^phi), made again at each link by correction.asked from that link's own rows. Not the raw-state alternative.
row_requests.site: the link's own feed-forward merge (33). Nothing is asked of a builder at the layer's last merge.
row_requests.support_note: All seven supports stand, discovery-15-channel-h1 among them, as in the primary chain. At this run's one link, feed-forward 33, 12 of the fourteen builders rest mostly on that support in the step-3 reading; it is 8 J under the regime's boundary, and Performance's card-1 direct terms put its feed-forward-33 term at -1.70 beside -2.73 to -5.03 for the other six. Kept as descriptions: no margin and no projected difference becomes a multiplier, an exclusion or a target, and no auxiliary observation becomes a support.
row_requests.correspondence: alpha, made at the link: each builder's nearest mixture of the seven supports at the incoming features, the builder's as the original has them against the supports' as the ORIGINAL file has them; held fixed for that link's solve. Recorded with the link's request.
row_requests.native_execution: The request same-line-sign-original kept was measured on the registered recordings. Each link's request is made in the reading its solve's rows are in (controlled-bf16-4's passes, as generated, card 0): the builders' incoming states from the link's own rows, the supports' states before and after the merge and every row's origin from the original file's own reading in that same execution (controlled-bf16-1/baseline, which every solve counts from). Link 33's is compared with the recordings' request and the difference recorded; the recordings' file is kept as it is.
row_requests.exclusions: No case has two answers among the builders and supports. discovery-10-channel-h1 (a builder) and discovery-10-channel-h3 (a correct member) answer one question and are kept in one fold.
row_requests.unsupported_cells: Every registered place and prompt position of the fifteen wrong fitting members except the fourteen builders' sign rows: no target is known there and none is invented; they carry no term and are not called agreement. Among them the sign row of expanded-001-h3. All thirty are in the outcome reading.
row_requests.read_by: correction.asked makes links/<link>/asked.npz and asked.json; correction.rows_asked hands it to the solve after checking its hash, the rows' hash and the starting state's hash.

solver.each_link_records: links/<link>/candidate/record.json keeps the hashes of correction.py and tube.py its solve ran, the card it was solved on and, for a solve made on another machine, what laid and solved it (made_with.solved_elsewhere).

hypothesis: Marcos's, for round two: a capability leaves a recurring difference between the traces of correct and wrong answers, and editing the weights where that recurring difference lives repairs the capability. Here, for the one decision the readings have isolated: six feed-forward merges, 29 to 34, write the sign's margin together, and feed-forward 33's direct term is the one graded in the question's numbers on the failing wording. If the recurring difference at the sign's row is carried by what that one matrix reads, then correcting it alone, from the original, takes the subtracting answers' sign rows along the correct answers' path without the five other edits, while every correct member's computation stays where the original has it.
why_this_direction: Step 5 asks for the edit where the recurring difference lives, and the step-3 reading for this decision is made (same-line-sign-original). The primary chain is one configuration of that edit. Astra's specification names what the evidence so far leaves open and gives each open point its own bounded construction, with one finalized candidate each. This one: the choice of six links was made before any single-site native result existed. The direct-term attribution singled out feed-forward 33, the single-site candidate was declared and then replaced before a row was read, and Performance's fixed-denominator arithmetic warned that one site's term, transplanted, may leave the margin on the minus side, which is arithmetic that leaves out the changed computation downstream and is no forecast. So whether one site suffices is not known. This run asks it natively, under the contract the chain is read by. It runs beside the primary because none of the four constructions has a result and Marcos asked for several at once. It is not chosen because another run's numbers were bad: no solve of any of the four has finished.
repeating_pattern_check: What has happened more than once. (a) One construction was run while the others waited on its result: Marcos named it on November 12 and again on November 13. This run is declared beside the primary and the two other constructions before any of the four has a candidate, so none is chosen or shaped by another's outcome, and each is reported whatever it reads. (b) A path was declared without its cost measured: the primary's first solve did not fit card 0. Every solve of this run is placed, before it starts, on a card that holds it, and its record says which. (c) Inputs were combined without saying so. This run's first link reads rows another run kept; they are named with their hash, were read on card 0 in the reading every solve here counts from, and are held against the link's state and matrix before the solve. (d) One site was taken for the whole path: three earlier candidates each changed one matrix, and my single-site declaration assumed 33 before the six merges were read together. This run does not repeat that by assumption and does not assume the opposite either: one site and six are both made, by one rule each, and compared on the model's own answers. (e) A reading was taken for a verdict: this link's solve readings, held folds included, are construction readings; the result is the final file's own answers and traces. (f) A configuration that fails is this configuration failing.
what_went_wrong_before: The first attempt at round two was deleted because it never built on the overlap. In this line: B and C at attention 17 asked the wrong group's mean for the cohort's whole-state difference and correct answers acquired errors; my claim that a key at the sign's row leaves correct answers alone was withdrawn after Performance read it; the joined reading's prediction of specificity was not met; the same-line reading's first read stopped before any reading on a one-point reference and was fixed. For this run in particular: I declared a single-site candidate at feed-forward 33 before reading what the six merges do together, which Performance's direct terms then showed, and before asking what a solve costs at a 12288-wide input, which Performance measured; Astra replaced that declaration before any row was read. And the request's known weakness, the near-boundary support, was found by Performance after I had named only the concentration. rule.reference: The frozen output-norm reference correction-at-19 made from the original model, read only, with the index hash above. Its direction and size weights are every link's weights. Its group cells are left out of the sum by a view made in memory (correction.without_groups); the saved arrays are untouched. The seven supports are a local comparison for the fourteen sign rows, not a replacement cohort or reference.
rule.objective: At link L, with u the unit state and l the log of its size after a merge, d the movement of a member's own mean from the ORIGINAL file's computation on the same recorded text, w_f = 0.5/S_f the reference's weight of a form, n_w and n_c the wrong and correct members among the answers summed over: E_L = sum over the builders i among them of (w_direction/n_w) ||d_u(i, sign row) - q_i||^2 + (w_size/n_w) (d_l(i, sign row) - s_i)^2 at feed-forward L's merge; plus, at feed-forward L's merge and at layer L's last merge (raw, as the reference reads it), the sum over forms f, over the correct members i and over every registered place p and every prompt position t of (w_f/n_c) ||d_f(i, p or t)||^2. Nothing else: no cell of either group, no term on a wrong member's other rows, no separate protection term, no bound and no bringing-back phase. n_w counts every wrong member of the part, the unsupported one included: fifteen in the last solve, with fourteen requests.
rule.request: T^phi_i = phi(h_i-, as the link's starting state has it) + sum_k alpha_ik [phi(H_k+) - phi(H_k-)] over the seven supports at their own sign rows, the supports' two states the ORIGINAL file's; alpha measured at the incoming features and held fixed for the link. (q_i, s_i) is T^phi_i less the original's own features after the merge at that row, the size's part over the root of the weights' ratio (6.6508510517827295): the movement asked, counted from the original as every movement is. At this run's one link, feed-forward 33 from the original, it is the request the single-site run declared, in the native reading. A least-squares request: no claim that the target can be attained, no dose, nothing taken from a score.
rule.counted_from: Every row of every link is counted from the original file's own output at the same row (tube.counted_from on controlled-bf16-1's baseline through controlled-bf16-4): a member's movement at a place is the mean over its steps there of each row's own movement, and a prompt position's is that row's. Each builder has one row at place 168.
rule.data_roles: The fitting half only, 15 wrong and 15 correct, in three folds with every case's answers in one (correction.case_folds: tube.picks' folds, then each answer to the fold of its case's first answer in the fitting order; it moves discovery-10-channel-h3 from fold 0 to fold 1, beside its sibling). Wrong [5, 5, 5], correct [4, 6, 5], builders [4, 5, 5]. Two folds solved on and the third read, in rotation, and all thirty for the last solve. A fold is read on its own builders' requests and its own correct members' terms. No no-fit answer supplies anything; the twelve auxiliary replays are not read; reserved-40b stays sealed.
rule.held_score: S = sum over the two groups g and the three folds k of n[g, k]/N[g] x E[g, k], E[g, k] being held fold k's reading of group g (the requests are the wrong group's; each correct member's own error the correct group's), n[g, k] the group's answers in the fold and N[g] = 15 (Astra, records/retrospectives/2026-11-12-ridge-end-astra.md). The folds no longer hold the two groups in one proportion, and the folds' mean by their numbers of answers would weigh a group's members differently from fold to fold. The same S selects the setting and counts the allowance.
rule.rows: The first link (33) reads the rows `chain.first_rows` names: the fitting answers' recorded tokens through the original, as controlled-bf16-4's passes read (the prompt at once, the answer's tokens one at a time), on card 0 under its lock: the matrix's input (12288 wide) and the state its merge adds to at 14,592 answer rows and 5,159 prompt positions. The model is only read.
rule.candidate: Per link: correction.chosen with that link's fourteen requests, the two correct-member requests and both groups' cells left out (members_only). Three paths go down the ridges in step from the first ridge; every written state a path accepts is a setting, named by its ridge and its round, and its score is S read on the answers each path was not solved on; the least score is taken, the unchanged matrix among the settings, with the existing ties. All thirty are then solved on once down the same ridges to that setting. One matrix a link; none is made again whatever it reads. Nothing of an edited answer, a token score or an auxiliary case enters any choice.
rule.paths_end: Every ridge from the first down to the unit is made. Below the unit the paths end at whichever comes first: the existing ends (a linear solve with no finite step; nothing of any fold's sum left; a ridge at which states were written and neither any fold nor S read less than before; the last halved ridge not smaller than RESOLVED of the unit), or the allowance: two ridges in a row at which no accepted setting, at any of its rounds, scored under the least S before that ridge (Astra, records/retrospectives/2026-11-12-ridge-end-astra.md). A new least starts the count again; one fold reading less by itself does not; a ridge at which nothing was written has no setting and counts as one without a new least. The allowance is a budget of exploration: a path it ends can miss a later ridge that would have scored less, and each link's record says which end ended its paths.
rule.numerical_work: The solver's rounds, with three things declared for this width. (a) A second ridge on a round's own step, read from the merges themselves (solve's damping='measured'): the step is solved in the first-order model, the sum is read through the merges at the step, and what the first order left out, over the step's squared length, is the least second ridge under which the model lies no lower than the merges; it only rises along a path. It changes how the rounds reach a ridge's minimum, not the sum, the ridge or what a setting is. (b) A linear solve is sped in the eigenvectors the reference cells' action reads: that action is a gram of 960 rows of inputs a merge (2 groups x 480 places), 1,920 over a feed-forward's two frames, so it reads at most that many of the 12,288 directions; on the others the same operator is the ridge alone and is applied as that. No value is dropped by its size. The command holds it once a path against the product over every eigenvector. (c) A step is multiplied into the rows the sum reads: the correct members' rows and the fourteen sign rows, about half; at a row no term reads, what a step does is weighed by nothing. The command finds them from the sum's own quadratic and holds that quadratic against the one over every row. A trial is still written in BF16 and read through the native merge expression on every row, and taken only when the whole sum on the answers solved on is strictly less. The three folds are walked in one process. A link's solve runs on a card that holds it, fixed before that solve starts by which card can hold it and is free and never by a result: a rented RTX 5090 (32 GB; Marcos's authorization above) from one file of what `chosen` takes, laid on this machine by the head of `candidate` under the verifier (records/development/2026-11-13-rented-solve/bundle.py, Performance's), the matrix and `chosen`'s record returned and the link's record finished here (correction.returned); or a card of this machine once a solve at this width fits one. At a 12288-wide input the solve as written does not fit 16 GB (runs/sign-chain-29-34-original/logs/29-candidate.out). The link's record says which card solved it and which files ran. Another card's arithmetic rounds differently, as two runs of one declared solve on one card do; the difference between cards is not measured and is a named limit of setting the four candidates side by side.
rule.write: Only the run's one file inside this run is written (correction.write_link): a copy of the original made at the first written link, then each link's candidate where its matrix lies, each value one the file's BF16 holds. After each writing the whole file is checked: every written link's matrix holds its candidate value for value, and every byte outside those matrices is the original's. links/<link>/written.json keeps the file's hash, which the next link starts from. The original file is only read.
rule.own_reading: Astra's contract (records/development/2026-11-12-path-forward/READING-OF-FEEDFORWARD-33.md, extended for the chain at 9f355823), implemented by weight-research-perfomance on the finalized file and hash: the fixed-input site readings from each link's matrix, the candidate's own answers and full traces on all thirty prompts on card 1 (the primary result), and the original on the candidate's changed text. Nothing in those readings selects or changes a link. The manifest that contract asks for is `row_requests`, each link's asked.json, `correct_members` and `correction_reference`. The four candidates (the primary chain and the three constructions beside it) are read by the same contract and reported side by side; their fitting sums cover different things and are not compared as scores (Astra's specification).
rule.scope: One matrix, from the original, on the recordings' text. It does not solve the correspondence of a model's own changed text to the original computation and is not the on-policy loop. It does not open the no-fit or reserved evaluations. It is not a reproduction of D1 or of the deleted A2 (Astra's specification maps both and names what is missing).
rule.storage: The link keeps its request and its candidate (76 MB); the run keeps one model file (9.3 GB). The rows it reads are another run's and stay there. Once the link is written and checked the candidate matrix goes to the bucket with torad-research and is verified there; records stay in the repository. The disk is read before each command.

coordinates_and_weights.derivation: The frozen reference's scales S_direction 1268.5365669493656 and S_size 28.67797931944294: a form weighs w_f = 0.5/S_f, 3.9415e-04 for the direction and 1.7435e-02 for the size, the same at every merge, place and link. The joint features' size coordinate is the log size times the root of w_size/w_direction (6.6508510517827295).
coordinates_and_weights.scales_with: The original model, its full original reference and the native terminal transform. Another source needs its own reference.

request_target.derivation: The step-3 run fixes who is asked and against whom (its fourteen builders, seven supports, each one's sign row) and the construction; its kept request at this merge has lengths 0.062 to 0.195 at feed-forward 33. This run's own request is made by correction.asked from the rows the link reads and the original file's reading, as `rule.request` says, and recorded with its hash and its distance from the kept one. Nothing of it is scaled, capped or rounded.
request_target.scales_with: The supports, the correspondence at each link's incoming state, the merge, the prefix and the text of the answers.

request_rows.derivation: The frozen registration lays each of the fourteen builders' sign rows alone at place 168 (checked again by correction.asked at every link of this run): at that place a builder's mean is its one row, so the request asked of the member there is the row's own.

request_weight.derivation: A request weighs the reference's own cell of the wrong group at that merge and place, w_f, over the number of wrong members among the answers summed over: 10 on the two folds a path is solved on, 5 on the fold it is read on, 15 for the last solve (fourteen requests, each at w_f/15). Not rebalanced by margin, support, parameter count or number of rows (Astra).
request_weight.scales_with: The reference's weights and the number of wrong members in each sum.

correct_member_weight.derivation: A correct member's squared own error at a place weighs w_f/n_c with n_c the number of correct members among the answers summed over: 11, 9 and 10 on the pairs of folds solved on, 4, 6 and 5 on the folds read, 15 for the last solve. The group's own cell is left out, so this is counted once.
correct_member_weight.scales_with: The reference's weights and the number of correct members in each sum.

prompt_position_weight.derivation: One prompt position of a correct member weighs what one registered answer place of that member weighs, w_f/n_c: the convention that diagnostic exercised and Astra's specification of the member objective kept. A convention between two units, named as one, and no multiplier to tune.
prompt_position_weight.scales_with: The reference's weights, the number of correct members summed over, and each prompt's number of positions.

ridge_unit.derivation: Per link, correction.unit_of on the reference's unmodified cells at the matrix the link starts from over all thirty fitting answers' rows that link keeps: the trace of the direction cells' action on the inputs times the mean squared learned scale, plus the size cells' curvature trace over the output width, over the input width. Computed by each link's command and recorded; no value from another matrix or link is used. A scale the search is counted in, not a claim about the sum's curvature.
ridge_unit.scales_with: The link's rows, the matrix's shape (12288 by 1536), the learned merge scale and the reference's weights.

first_ridge.derivation: Per link, the largest power of two times the unit not above 2||s||^2/(RESOLVED x E), with E the whole sum on all thirty at the link's start and s the slope of E/2 there (correction.strongest). Computed by each link's command and recorded with its inputs.
first_ridge.scales_with: The link's requests, where the prefix has left the correct members, the initial slope, the unit and the arithmetic's resolution.

ridge_spacing.derivation: The solver halves the ridge from one stage to the next (PATH = 1), each stage starting from the last written state. The search's grain, the same for every matrix; a valley between two powers can be missed, and the record keeps every stage.
ridge_spacing.scales_with: Nothing of the data: a finer grain costs proportionally more stages.

work_limits.derivation: The solver's own constants as each record keeps them (tube.EFFORT: at most 40 accepted rounds a stage, and 400 conjugate-gradient iterations a round's linear solve, as 10 passes of 40 where cells have radii and one run of 400 where none has; RESOLVED, the root of float32's rounding, ends a stage whose round falls by no more than that part of its starting sum). They were set on the solver's calibration at other matrices and are not measured for these: they limit work and do not shape the sum. Whether they bind is recorded per stage; a stage that ends at a limit is work not finished and no statement about what a longer solve would reach.
work_limits.scales_with: The local curvature at each matrix and the ridge.

second_ridge.derivation: No number: at each round the second ridge is (the sum read through the merges at the solved step, less the first-order model's value there) over the step's squared length, when that difference is more than RESOLVED of the sum, and the step is solved again where it exceeds the one it was solved with; it only rises along a path. On correction-members-at-17-original's sum (the record named): twelve rounds from that run's candidate at 2^-5 went from 9.3334e-05 to 9.0246e-05 in 108.1 s with no second ridge, nine of them taking a sixteenth of their step or less, and to 8.4482e-05 in 33.7 s with the measured one, every step whole; the whole path from 2^23 to 2^-5, walked twice, took 361.6 and 372.2 s against the run's own final solve's 541.7 s, the two walks within 4.5e-05 of the sum at every stage's end down to 2^-2 and 0.9% to 2.4% apart at 2^-3 to 2^-5. What it costs is named with it: at 2^-4 and 2^-5 its stages used all forty rounds and ended 9% to 12% above the run's own refit, so at the weakest ridges a stage can end at the round limit short of where the solve without it ended. Declared for this run, as for the primary chain, as the solver's owner's numerical decision (Astra's record on the paths' end leaves it to this seat).
second_ridge.scales_with: How far the merges depart from their first order at a step, which depends on the matrix, the ridge and the step.

step_acceptance.derivation: Each BF16-written trial is read through the native merge expression on every row and taken only when the whole sum E on the answers solved on is strictly less; otherwise the part of the step is halved down to no written movement. No bound and no held reading vetoes a step; held folds choose the setting only.
step_acceptance.scales_with: The file's BF16 grid and the proposed change.

allowance_of_ridges.derivation: Astra's: K = 1 + the longest run of completed ridges without a new least held score that was followed by a new least, over every accepted setting of the three archived paths (correction-at-19, correction-at-17-original, correction-members-at-17-original; hashes in the record named). That longest run is one ridge, in the third: least scores 3.4960e-04, 3.5221e-04 and 3.4560e-04 at 2^-3, 2^-4 and 2^-5. So K = 2. Replayed on those tables by the solver's tests: the three selections are kept.
allowance_of_ridges.scales_with: The recovery behaviour of the solver, the objective, the data and the ridge spacing. Frozen for this chain; not changed from its outcomes; another model or construction needs its own.

held_score.derivation: S as `rule.held_score` gives it, with the folds' group counts wrong [5, 5, 5] and correct [4, 6, 5] over 15 and 15: a held fold's request terms count by 5/15 each, its correct members' terms by 4/15, 6/15 and 5/15. No weight of ours: it is the whole per-member objective over the held answers.

solve_geometry.derivation: The eigenbasis that speeds a round's linear solves and the measure a writing is nearest in are made from the reference's unmodified cells on the rows solved on (correction.basis_of). The action is a gram of one row of inputs a cell, so its rank is at most the number of cells of the merges read (1,920 here) whatever the width; Performance measured 1,732 values above what a double factoring resolves, of at most 1,920, at a 6144-wide feed-forward matrix (the record named) and 958 of at most 960 at attention 17, 2,048 wide (the record beside it). The linear solve and the measure use the eigenvectors of the 1,920 largest values and the ridge alone on every other direction: the same operator, not a truncation by size. They change how fast a solve arrives and which BF16 neighbour a writing prefers, not what is solved.
solve_geometry.scales_with: The rows solved on, the reference's weights and the number of places and merges read.

prediction: Stated before any request or solve of this run. (1) The residual at this merge is carried by what the matrix reads: at the setting, in each of the three folds, the request terms of the builders the path was not solved on read less than at the start. (2) It is made where the traces differ: the held S falls, and in each fold the held correct members' terms rise by less than that fold's held requests fall; in Performance's fixed-input reading the matrix moves its merge's output more at the fourteen wrong sign rows than at the correct members' sign rows. (3) On the model's own answers, read under Astra's contract: the builders' sign margins move toward the plus, by less than under the six-link chain, because five of the six writers stay the original's; no originally correct fitting answer acquires an error in either use of energy, and fewer rows of the correct answers move than under the chain. would_weaken_it: Of (1) and (2): held requests that do not fall in any fold, a selection that keeps the unchanged matrix, or correct rows that move as much as the wrong sign rows, say that this residual, with this support and correspondence, is not carried by what this matrix reads in a form the solve finds on these rows. revisions.what_changes: rule.numerical_work (b), and where the folds' rows lie. The vectors a linear solve is sped in, and a writing's measure is made from, are read off the rows of inputs the reference cells' action is the gram of: the right singular vectors of the stack of those rows (960 a merge read, each times the root of its cell's weight), with the squares of its singular values.
